title: How a Judge Got to 110 Years for Allen Stanford

lines.say: March sixth, two thousand twelve. A Houston jury convicts Allen Stanford on thirteen of fourteen counts.
lines.show: March 6, 2012. A Houston jury convicts Allen Stanford on 13 of 14 counts.

lines.say: The one acquittal: nine thousand dollars in Super Bowl tickets for an Antiguan regulator.
lines.show: The one acquittal: $9,000 in Super Bowl tickets for an Antiguan regulator.

lines.say: Judge David Hittner called it one of the most egregious frauds ever presented to a trial jury in federal court.
Twenty years for the fraud conspiracy. Twenty on each of four wire fraud counts. Five on each of two obstruction counts. All consecutive.
lines.show: 20 years for the fraud conspiracy. 20 on each of four wire fraud counts. Five on each of two obstruction counts. All consecutive.

lines.say: One hundred ten years, out of a possible two hundred thirty. Plus a five point nine billion dollar money judgment.
lines.show: 110 years, out of a possible 230. Plus a $5.9 billion money judgment.

lines.say: The Fifth Circuit affirmed. Stanford, it wrote, sat atop a massive Ponzi scheme.
lines.show: The Fifth Circuit affirmed. Stanford, it wrote, "sat atop a massive Ponzi scheme."

scene.q: Stanford sat atop a massive Ponzi scheme

lines.say: Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
